name: @triffon/moodle-mcp

tools.name: configure
tools.description: Set this server's configuration for this session: the Moodle site (url; a new one is added to the server's sites and kept, a known one becomes active, see use_site), whether the browser runs without a window (headless), how student tools view and do things (trail) and the browser profile folder (profileDir). It can also narrow the kinds of tools (scopes), the role (role) or access to read only (access) and tighten how others' data reaches you (studentData), never the other way: widening is the person's, in the client's configuration. Each is optional; only those given change. The URL is checked to be a Moodle site. Kept in memory only, but for a new site, which stays among the server's sites. Returns the effective configuration, as server_info.

url.description: The Moodle site's URL, or any page of it (a course URL works: the site is read from it)

headless.description: Run the browser without a window (logging in always shows one)

trail.description: How student tools view and do things: realistic (real pages, human pace; Moodle logs views and completion) or fast

profileDir.description: Absolute folder for the browser profile that keeps the Moodle session; outside the server's folder

scopes.description: Narrow the kinds of tools for this session: a profile (teacher, student, content) or scopes (content, student-data, grading, communication, as-student, browser). Only fewer than now, never more

studentData.description: Tighten how others' data reaches you for this session (block is strictest). Only stricter than now, never looser

role.description: Keep only one role's tools for this session (teacher or student), from all; never back to all

access.description: read: keep only the tools that change nothing in Moodle for this session; never back to write

tools.name: login
tools.description: Make sure there is a Moodle session. If there is one, returns the logged-in user at once. Otherwise opens a browser window at the site's login page and waits until the person logs in there themselves (the server never sees their password), then returns the user. Call it when another tool reports a missing or expired session.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the person to log in, in seconds (default 300)

tools.name: logout
tools.description: End the person's Moodle session in the server's browser, so someone else can log in (another account: login opens the window again). Only Moodle's session ends: a single sign-on provider may keep its own and log the same person back in. Only when the person asks.

tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Tell who the logged-in person is: user id, username, full name, email, language, time zone, first and last access, and the site. With courseId, also their roles in that course and whether they can edit it and grade in it.

courseId.description: A course id (from list_courses) to also get the person's roles and abilities there

tools.name: get_site_info
tools.description: What the Moodle site says about itself: its name, URL, language, how people log in (its own form, guest access, single sign-on providers) and whether it's in maintenance; readable before logging in. With courseId, also the activity and resource types the person can add to that course (none if they can't edit it): take the type for create_activity from here. Moodle shows its version only to administrators, so it isn't given.

courseId.description: A course to list the activity types that can be added to it

tools.name: list_courses
tools.description: List the Moodle courses the logged-in person is enrolled in (as teacher or student), with their ids, names, category, URL, visibility, dates and, where Moodle tracks it, the person's progress: only as a student, in courses with completion tracking (a teacher gets none; students' progress is in get_completion_report). Filter by dates with classification.

classification.description: Which courses by their dates: "all" (default), "inprogress", "future" or "past"

tools.name: get_course_structure
tools.description: Get a Moodle course's sections and activities: ids, names, types, URLs, visibility, whether the person can open each one, restrictions and, where Moodle tracks it, the person's completion: only as a student, on activities with completion tracking (a teacher gets none; students' completion is in get_completion_report). With details, also each activity's dates and restriction text as the course page shows them. Takes the course id from list_courses.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

details.description: Also read the course page for each activity's dates and restriction text (slower; default false)

tools.name: get_activity_content
tools.description: Read a content activity as a person would, so Moodle logs the view: a page's or label's text, a book's chapters, a URL resource's target, or a file resource's or folder's files (as links). Takes the id and type from get_course_structure. With the realistic trail it reads page by page at a reader's pace and reports progress.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

type.description: The activity's type, as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: list_participants
tools.description: List a course's participants with their roles and groups, as the participants page does: people as aliases when the server pseudonymizes, never emails or profile fields. Filter by role, group, or those who haven't accessed the course since a date (inactiveSince). A page at a time: limit participants (50 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others.

role.description: Only this role's, by its id (as the participants' roles give it)

group.description: Only this group's members, by its id from list_groups

inactiveSince.description: Only those who haven't accessed the course since this date (ISO 8601)

limit.description: How many participants (50 by default, up to 500)

offset.description: How many participants to skip first (0 by default)

tools.name: list_groups
tools.description: List the groups of a course the person can see, with their members (as aliases when the server pseudonymizes). Their ids are what the reports' group filter takes.

tools.name: list_potential_users
tools.description: Find users the person may enrol in a course by manual enrolment, as the "Enrol users" dialog does: matching search in their name or the identity fields the site shows (up to 100 when empty). People as aliases when the server pseudonymizes, never their emails. Enrol them with enrol_users.

search.description: Part of a name, an email, an ID number…

tools.name: enrol_users
tools.description: Enrol users in a course by manual enrolment, as the "Enrol users" dialog does: with a role (the enrolment's default unless roleId), from start (now) until end (the enrolment's default duration). Takes them as list_potential_users gives them. Those already enrolled keep their enrolment, with the new dates. Confirm with the person first.

users.description: The participants' aliases, as the reading tools give them when the server pseudonymizes

userIds.description: The participants' user ids, when the server shows names

roleId.description: The role to give, as list_participants' roles give it

tools.name: unenrol_user
tools.description: Unenrol someone from a course: removes every enrolment of theirs the person may remove, with their roles and group memberships in the course; removed and kept name the enrolment methods. Their work in the course stays in Moodle but they lose access. Confirm with the person first.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: set_user_roles
tools.description: Set a participant's roles in a course, as the participants page's roles column does: gives the roles in roleIds the person may assign and takes away the other ones they may assign; roles from elsewhere stay. Returns the roles afterwards. Confirm with the person first.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

roleIds.description: Role ids, as list_participants' roles give them

tools.name: set_group_members
tools.description: Add and remove members of a group, as its members page does: only the course's participants can be added. Takes them as list_participants gives them: aliases (add, remove) when the server pseudonymizes, else user ids (addIds, removeIds). Returns the members afterwards. Confirm with the person first.

add.description: Aliases to add, when the server pseudonymizes

remove.description: Aliases to remove, when the server pseudonymizes

addIds.description: User ids to add, when the server shows names

removeIds.description: User ids to remove, when the server shows names

tools.name: create_group
tools.description: Create a group in a course with Moodle's group form. Add its members with set_group_members. Returns its id. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

enrolmentKey.description: A key that enrols students straight into this group with self enrolment

tools.name: update_group
tools.description: Change a group's name, description, ID number or enrolment key; what isn't given stays. Confirm with the person first.

groupId.description: The group's id, as list_groups gives it

enrolmentKey.description: A key that enrols students straight into this group with self enrolment

tools.name: delete_group
tools.description: Delete a group; its members stay in the course. Activities set to work by groups lose it. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

groupId.description: The group's id, as list_groups gives it

tools.name: list_groupings
tools.description: List a course's groupings (sets of groups an activity can be limited to) with their groups' ids. Needs the right to manage groups.

tools.name: create_grouping
tools.description: Create a grouping in a course with Moodle's form; give it its groups with set_grouping_groups. Returns its id. Confirm with the person first.

tools.name: delete_grouping
tools.description: Delete a grouping; its groups stay. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

groupingId.description: The grouping's id, as list_groupings gives it

tools.name: set_grouping_groups
tools.description: Make a grouping's groups exactly groupIds, adding and removing as its page does; groups of other courses are left out and named. Returns its groups afterwards. Confirm with the person first.

groupingId.description: The grouping's id, as list_groupings gives it

tools.name: auto_create_groups
tools.description: Split a course's participants into groups at once, as Moodle's "Auto-create groups" does: count groups, or groups of count members, named by naming (# a number, @ a letter), filled at random or by name or ID number (or left empty), from a role (students by default), a cohort, a grouping or a group, optionally into an existing or new grouping. preview: true shows the groups and members Moodle would make and creates nothing: do that first, then give its seed back to create those same groups. Members as aliases when the server pseudonymizes. Confirm with the person first.

by.description: groups: count groups; members: groups of count members

naming.description: The groups' names: # becomes their number, @ a letter ("Group @")

allocation.description: random by default; none leaves them empty

roleId.description: Only this role (0: every role); students by default

notInGroup.description: Only participants in no group yet

noSmallGroups.description: With members: spread a last group that would be too small over the others

newGrouping.description: Or in a new grouping of this name

seed.description: A preview's seed, to create those same groups

tools.name: import_groups
tools.description: Create groups from a local CSV file, as Moodle's "Import groups" does: a groupname column, and optionally description, enrolmentkey, groupidnumber, groupingname (made when missing) and enablemessaging. Moodle creates the groups without members. Returns the new groups and Moodle's messages for the rows it skipped. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

file.description: An absolute local path to the CSV

tools.name: list_enrolment_methods
tools.description: List how people can enrol in a course, in the order Moodle tries them: each method's type, name, whether it's on, how many it enrolled, the role it gives and, for self enrolment and guest access, whether it asks for a key (never the key), dates and limit.

tools.name: set_enrolment_method
tools.description: Change an enrolment method with its form, by its id or the course's first of a type (methodType "self": added when the course has none and Moodle offers it): turn it on or off, its key, dates, role, limit and welcome message. Only what's given changes. Returns the method afterwards (never the key). Opens or closes the course to people: confirm with the person first.

methodType.description: Or the method's type, such as "self" or "guest"

key.description: Self enrolment or guest access key; empty to remove it

start.description: From when, ISO 8601; "none" to remove it

end.description: Until when, ISO 8601; "none" to remove it

welcomeMessage.description: Self enrolment: send this welcome message

noWelcome.description: Self enrolment: send no welcome message

tools.name: get_grader_report
tools.description: Read everyone's grades in a course as the grader report shows them, in one group when given: its columns (grade items, categories, the course total) and a row per participant (an alias when the server pseudonymizes) with their grades.

group.description: Only this group's members, by its id from list_groups

tools.name: get_completion_report
tools.description: Read a course's progress report: every participant's completion (an alias when the server pseudonymizes) of every activity that tracks it, in one group when given; whether it's manual or automatic, and whether a teacher overrode it.

group.description: Only this group's members, by its id from list_groups

tools.name: get_activity_report
tools.description: Read a course's activity report: per activity, how many times it was viewed, by how many people and when last, from the logs (between from and until when given). Counts only, no one's name. Activities nobody viewed come with zero.

tools.name: get_participation_report
tools.description: Read an activity's participation report: everyone with a role (all the roles it offers, unless roleId) and how many actions they made there (views or posts only with action; since a date with since); those who did nothing come with 0. People as aliases when the server pseudonymizes.

tools.name: get_course_logs
tools.description: Read a course's logs, newest first, as its logs report lists them: by a user (an alias when the server pseudonymizes), an activity, a kind of action and a time span, a page at a time: limit entries (50 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others. Each entry: when, who, who it was about, where, what happened (Moodle's longer description only with includeDescriptions). Never IP addresses.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

offset.description: How many entries to skip first, newest first (0 by default)

includeDescriptions.description: Also each entry's description, Moodle's sentence about it (longer; default false)

tools.name: set_grade
tools.description: Set a participant's grade in a grade item, as the gradebook's single view does: a manual item takes it; an activity's or a category's is overridden (until override false takes it off). Also feedback and excluding it from the totals. The grade as text: points ("7.5"), a scale item, or "none" to empty it. Students may see it: confirm with the person first.

itemId.description: The grade item, as get_gradebook_setup or get_grader_report gives it

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

feedback.description: No aliases in it, since the student reads it

override.description: false: take an activity's or category's override off

tools.name: export_grades
tools.description: Save a course's grades into a local folder as Moodle exports them for a teacher: a spreadsheet (xlsx, ods), CSV or XML, with the items, group, display and feedback chosen. The file names every participant: only with names in clear (the server's student data level), since a file can't be pseudonymized.

tools.name: override_completion
tools.description: Set a participant's completion of an activity as a teacher does from the progress report (an override, shown as such). Takes the participant as get_completion_report gives them. Returns the state saved. Changes the participant's progress: confirm with the person first.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id)

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: get_course_completion_criteria
tools.description: Read what completes a course, from its "Course completion" settings: activities, other courses, a date, days enrolled, unenrolment, a course grade, self completion, roles that mark it, how they combine, what the form offers, whether completion is on and whether the criteria are locked. Course completion, not activity completion (get_completion_report).

tools.name: set_course_completion_criteria
tools.description: Set a course's completion criteria: a criterion given replaces that kind's settings, one in remove goes, one not given stays; overall says whether all criteria or any one complete the course. Activities need completion tracking, roles the right to mark completion (get_course_completion_criteria's offered lists both). Once someone has met a criterion Moodle locks them: unlock deletes every participant's course completion data first (not their activity completion). Returns the criteria. Confirm with the person first, and twice with unlock.

all.description: All of them (default) or any one

unlock.description: Unlock locked criteria first, deleting everyone's course completion data

tools.name: get_course_completion_status
tools.description: Read each participant's course completion from the course completion report: whether and when they completed the course, and each criterion met and when; participants as aliases when the server pseudonymizes. Some criteria (a grade, a date, days enrolled) are worked out by Moodle's scheduled tasks, so a criterion just met may not show yet. A page at a time: limit participants (50 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

limit.description: How many participants (50 by default, up to 200)

offset.description: How many participants to skip first (0 by default)

tools.name: mark_course_complete
tools.description: Mark a participant's course completion by hand (an alias when the server pseudonymizes), as the course completion report's link does: the course's "Manual completion by others" criterion for a role the person holds. Moodle completes the course when the rest of the criteria allow it. Returns their completion afterwards. Confirm with the person first.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: get_choice_results
tools.description: Read a choice's responses as its report shows a teacher: each option with how many chose it and who (aliases when the server pseudonymizes), and who hasn't answered where the choice shows that. The report names people whatever the choice publishes to students.

choiceId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: get_survey_results
tools.description: Read what people answered in a feedback or a questionnaire, as its reports show a teacher: every response (who gave it, an alias when the server pseudonymizes, none when anonymous) and, per question, each response's answer (text redacted when pseudonymizing), the counts of a choice question's options and the average of numeric and rated ones. A questionnaire lists its responses only once someone has answered.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

type.description: The activity's type, as get_course_structure gives it; found when missing

tools.name: list_assignments
tools.description: List the assignments of a Moodle course: their ids (course module ids, for the other assignment tools), names, URLs, visibility and section. Takes the course id from list_courses.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

tools.name: get_submissions
tools.description: Get the participants' submissions to a Moodle assignment, a page at a time (limit participants, 25 by default, after skipping offset; more says whether there are others): who (an alias when the server pseudonymizes, else id and name), status (submitted; draft; new: a submission started but nothing in it yet; reopened; none: no submission at all), whether it needs grading, extensions, the participant's dates and, by default, the content (online text and file links; names and contact data in it redacted when pseudonymizing). Changes nothing, but Moodle logs it as the teacher viewing the grading pages, as it does for its own grader. Takes the assignment id from list_assignments.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (its course module id), as list_assignments gives it

includeContent.description: Include each submission's content: online text and file links (default true)

limit.description: How many participants (25 by default, up to 200)

offset.description: How many participants to skip first, in the grading table's order (0 by default)

tools.name: list_discussions
tools.description: List the discussions of a Moodle forum: subject, who started it and when, the last post's author and time, the number of replies (0: unanswered) and whether it's locked. A page at a time: limit discussions (30 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others. Takes the forum id from get_course_structure; read one with get_discussion.

forumId.description: The forum's id (its course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

limit.description: How many discussions (30 by default, up to 100)

offset.description: How many discussions to skip first, in the forum's order (0 by default)

tools.name: get_discussion
tools.description: Read a Moodle forum discussion's posts, oldest first, a page at a time (limit posts, 50 by default, after skipping offset; more says whether there are others): author (an alias when the server pseudonymizes), time, the post it replies to, the message as plain text (names and contact data redacted when pseudonymizing) and attachments. Takes the discussion id from list_discussions.

discussionId.description: The discussion id, as list_discussions gives it

limit.description: How many posts (50 by default, up to 200)

offset.description: How many posts to skip first, oldest first (0 by default)

tools.name: get_my_grades
tools.description: Get the logged-in person's grade report for a course: each grade item (with its activity id), category and the course total, with grade, range, percentage, weight, letter, feedback and contribution, as Moodle shows them. Takes the course id from list_courses.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

tools.name: download_file
tools.description: Save a file of the Moodle site to a local folder, with the person's session: a resource's or folder's file (get_activity_content), an assignment's brief file or submitted file (get_assignment, get_submissions), a forum attachment (get_discussion). Only URLs of the configured site's host (its media too: videos it serves outside Moodle); external links (YouTube…) are for other tools. Never overwrites: an existing name gets a number. Returns where it was saved.

url.description: The file's URL on the site, as the other tools give it (…/pluginfile.php/…)

destDir.description: Absolute local folder to save into; created if missing

tools.name: get_survey
tools.description: Read a survey (the questionnaire plugin, or Moodle's feedback) as the person: whether they can answer it now, its messages (completed, closed…), and every question on every page, with whether it's required and its fields (names, options).

activityId.description: The survey's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

type.description: The activity's type, as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: submit_survey
tools.description: Answer a survey and submit it, page by page as its form goes: responses maps field names (from get_survey) to values ("1"/"0" for checkboxes, an option's value for choices and selects, text otherwise). Every name is checked first; Moodle's complaints (a required question left out) come back by page. Usually one response per person: confirm the answers with the person first, and ask them for personal data instead of guessing.

activityId.description: The survey's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

type.description: The activity's type, as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: get_choice
tools.description: Read a choice activity (a poll) as the person sees it: its question, the options with their ids, whether it's open, whether several can be chosen and whether the answer can change, and the person's answer.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: answer_choice
tools.description: Answer a choice activity as the person, with one option (several where the choice allows them) by id from get_choice, as "Save my choice" does. Returns the choice afterwards. Answers as the person, and some choices don't allow changing it: confirm with the person first.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: get_lesson_page
tools.description: Read the page of a lesson the person is on (starting the lesson the first time): a content page with its buttons, a question with its fields, or the end with the score. Answer it with answer_lesson_page.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: answer_lesson_page
tools.description: Go on in a lesson as the person: press a content page's button (by its label, or by its position from 1), or answer a question page's fields by name (an option's value for choice and select, text for text). Returns Moodle's feedback, if any, and the next page; reaching the end ends the attempt. Answers count towards the lesson's grade and can't be taken back. With the realistic trail it pauses to read the page first.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

button.description: A content page's button, by its label

responses.description: A question page's answers: field name → value, as get_lesson_page gives the fields

tools.name: get_h5p_activity
tools.description: Read an H5P activity: its content type (the H5P library), whether Moodle tracks attempts, and the person's own attempts with their scores. Solving the content itself (it runs in a player) is for the browser fallback tools.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: get_scorm
tools.description: Read a SCORM activity as the person sees it: attempts allowed and made, grading method, the grade reported and each attempt's, and its SCOs (the package's parts) with the person's status and score in the last attempt. Use it before open_scorm, and after doing the package to see what Moodle recorded.

activityId.description: The SCORM activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: open_scorm
tools.description: Open a SCORM activity in Moodle's player, as the person, in the browser tools' tab: the last attempt continues unless newAttempt, at the first SCO unless scoId. Opening it starts an attempt in Moodle. Then do the package with the browser tools: browser_snapshot reads it (refs inside its frame start with f, like f2e9), browser_click, browser_type and browser_select act on them, browser_wait waits for its texts. Afterwards, check the result with get_scorm instead of assuming it. Nothing marks a SCORM done or graded but doing it.

activityId.description: The SCORM activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

scoId.description: The SCO to open, as get_scorm gives it; the first when missing

newAttempt.description: Start a new attempt instead of continuing the last one

tools.name: set_completion
tools.description: Mark the person's own completion of an activity with manual completion, done or not done, as its "Mark as done" button does. Activities that complete on their own (by viewing, grade, submission) can't be marked: Moodle says so. Doing it twice changes nothing.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: list_pending
tools.description: List what the logged-in person still has to do in a course: activities whose completion is tracked and not complete or, where completion isn't tracked, graded activities without a grade yet; with their dates, restrictions and whether they can be opened now. Takes the course id from list_courses.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

tools.name: get_activities_overview
tools.description: Moodle's activities overview of a course, as the person sees it: per activity, its columns (due date, submissions, what needs grading, attempts, the person's own grade, forum subscriptions…), by type or for every type in the course. For a teacher, the quickest way to see what's waiting to be graded (alert "Needs grading"); for a student, what's due and their results. Moodle 5 and later.

type.description: One activity type (assign, quiz, forum…; "resource" for every resource type); every type when missing

tools.name: list_deadlines
tools.description: What the person has to do by a date, from Moodle's calendar (submit an assignment, attempt a quiz…), in one course or all of them: from a week ago (overdue ones) to some days ahead. Each with its activity id, date, whether it's overdue and the action Moodle offers. Teachers get few such events: for what's waiting to be graded, use get_activities_overview.

courseId.description: One course; every course when missing

tools.name: get_course_updates
tools.description: What changed in a course's activities since a date (settings, content files, forum posts, submissions, attempts, grades…), as Moodle tracks it for the person, with each activity's name and type. Useful at the start of a session: what's new since last time.

since.description: ISO date and time; a week ago when missing

tools.name: get_quiz_info
tools.description: Read a quiz's page as the person: description, its rules (attempts allowed, grading method, time limit…), dates, overall feedback, the person's attempts (with their ids, in progress or finished, and grades) and whether they can start one now.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: start_quiz_attempt
tools.description: Start an attempt at a quiz, or continue the one in progress, as the quiz page's button does; returns the attempt's id and its questions with their fields and options. Starting uses up one of the attempts allowed, and a time limit starts running: confirm with the person first.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: get_quiz_attempt
tools.description: Read every question of an attempt in progress, page by page: text, images, fields with their options, and the answers saved so far.

attemptId.description: The attempt's id, as start_quiz_attempt or get_quiz_info gives it

tools.name: answer_quiz_questions
tools.description: Save answers in an attempt in progress, as the attempt's pages do; it doesn't finish the attempt. Each answer names a question's slot and its fields by name with the value to give: an option's value for choice and select fields, "1" or "0" for checkboxes, text for text fields. Returns the questions with their saved answers. With the realistic trail it pauses to read each page first.

attemptId.description: The attempt's id, as start_quiz_attempt or get_quiz_info gives it

responses.description: Field name → value, as get_quiz_attempt gives the fields

tools.name: finish_quiz_attempt
tools.description: Submit an attempt for grading, as "Submit all and finish" does: no answer can change afterwards. Returns the review when the quiz shows it. Final: confirm with the person first, after checking the answers with get_quiz_attempt.

attemptId.description: The attempt's id, as start_quiz_attempt or get_quiz_info gives it

tools.name: get_attempt_review
tools.description: Read a finished attempt's review, as far as the quiz shows it: status, marks and grade, and per question whether it was right, the mark, feedback and the right answer. Someone else's attempt (a teacher's view) names them by alias, and their written answers are redacted, when the server pseudonymizes.

attemptId.description: The attempt's id, as start_quiz_attempt or get_quiz_info gives it

tools.name: get_quiz_results
tools.description: Read a quiz's attempts as its grades report shows them: per attempt the participant (an alias when the server pseudonymizes), state, dates, grade and the mark per question; with responses, also each answer given (redacted when pseudonymizing). A page at a time: limit attempts (50 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

responses.description: Also the answer per question (default false)

limit.description: How many attempts (50 by default, up to 500)

offset.description: How many attempts to skip first, in the report's order (0 by default)

tools.name: get_quiz_statistics
tools.description: Read a quiz's statistics report, which tells which questions work: the quiz's figures (attempts, averages, median, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, internal consistency, error ratio, standard error) and per question its facility index, standard deviation, weights, discrimination index and efficiency, dubious ones marked; a random slot's questions and variants each with their own; with responses, how often each response was given (one page read per question). Figures as the report shows them. attempts chooses which attempts count; recalculate clears what Moodle stored. Aggregates only: no person.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

attempts.description: The quiz's grading method by default

recalculate.description: Calculate again now, for attempts finished since

responses.description: Also each question's analysis of responses

tools.name: set_quiz_override
tools.description: Give a participant their own quiz settings, as the quiz's user overrides do: open and close dates, time limit in minutes, or number of attempts (0 unlimited); what isn't given stays the quiz's. Takes the participant as list_participants gives them. Confirm with the person first.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: list_questions_to_grade
tools.description: List a quiz's questions that wait for grading by hand (essays…), each with how many to grade and the finished attempts whose answer needs it (by attempt id, with the participant as an alias when the server pseudonymizes). Read an answer with get_attempt_review; grade it with grade_quiz_question.

tools.name: grade_quiz_question

comment.description: No aliases in it, since the student reads it

tools.name: get_assignment

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: save_submission
tools.description: Save the logged-in student's submission to an assignment: its online text (HTML, replacing what was there) and files to add (absolute local paths). Doesn't submit it for grading when the assignment asks students to click submit: submit_assignment does. Returns the assignment as the student sees it. Changes the submission: confirm with the person first.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: submit_assignment
tools.description: Submit the saved submission for grading: it can't be changed afterwards unless the teacher reopens it. Final: confirm with the person first, after checking the submission with get_assignment.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

acceptStatement.description: The person accepts the site's submission statement

tools.name: get_rubric

comments.description: A marking guide's frequently used comments, in order

tools.name: grant_extension

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it

users.description: The participants' aliases, when the server pseudonymizes

userIds.description: The participants' user ids, when the server shows names

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it

users.description: The participants' aliases, as the reading tools give them when the server pseudonymizes

userIds.description: The participants' user ids, when the server shows names

tools.name: allocate_marker
tools.description: Allocate a marker (someone who can grade; several where the assignment uses several per submission) to participants' submissions, as the grading table's bulk action does; Moodle leaves submissions past marking alone. assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it

users.description: The participants' aliases, as the reading tools give them when the server pseudonymizes

userIds.description: The participants' user ids, when the server shows names

markers.description: The markers' aliases, when the server pseudonymizes

markerIds.description: The markers' user ids, when the server shows names

postId.description: The post to reply to, as get_discussion gives it

message.description: The message (HTML); no aliases in it, since people read it

fields.description: Other post form fields by name, e.g. {"pinned": true} for a teacher

tools.name: create_discussion

forumId.description: The forum's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

message.description: The message (HTML); no aliases in it, since people read it

embed.description: Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name:

subscribe.description: Subscribe to the discussion; Moodle's default when missing

fields.description: Other post form fields by name, e.g. {"pinned": true} for a teacher

tools.name: set_discussion_state
tools.description: Pin or unpin, lock or unlock a forum discussion, as the discussion list's menu does; what's already so is left alone. Returns the discussion as the forum lists it afterwards. Students see it: confirm with the person first.

forumId.description: The forum's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: set_discussion_subscription
tools.description: Subscribe the person to a forum discussion, or unsubscribe them, as the discussion list's toggle does: Moodle then emails them its new posts. What's already so is left alone. Returns the discussion as the forum lists it afterwards.

forumId.description: The forum's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: edit_post
tools.description: Change a forum post through Moodle's own form, as its author (within the site's editing time) or a moderator: its subject, message (HTML), and attachments to add or remove. message.description: HTML; no aliases in it, since people read it

embed.description: Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name:

tools.name: delete_post
tools.description: Delete a forum post and its replies through Moodle's own confirmation; a discussion's first post takes the whole discussion. Only a moderator deletes someone else's post or one with replies. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

tools.name: get_forum_grades
tools.description: Read the whole-forum grades of a forum graded as a whole, as its grader shows them: one per person it can grade (aliases when the server pseudonymizes), with how it's graded (points or scale) and who graded.

tools.name: grade_forum_user
tools.description: Give a participant their whole-forum grade, as the forum's grader does: points ("7"), a scale item, or "none" to take it away; notify sends them Moodle's notification. Students may see it: confirm with the person first.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: rate
tools.description: Rate a forum post, a glossary entry or a database record as the person, as the rating menu under it does: a scale item's name, or a number (a point scale's points); "none" takes the person's rating away. Returns the item's aggregate afterwards. Students may see it: confirm with the person first.

itemId.description: The post's, entry's or record's id

discussionId.description: For a forum post: its discussion

tools.name: get_workshop
tools.description: Read a workshop's phase and its report as a teacher sees it: every submission (author, title, grade once calculated) and every assessment (reviewer, the submission's author, the grade it gives, its weight, the grade for assessing). People as aliases when the server pseudonymizes. Empty lists before the submission phase, or for someone who can't see every submission.

tools.name: set_workshop_phase
tools.description: Switch a workshop to a phase (setup, submission, assessment, evaluation, closed), forwards or back, as its page's phase links do. Moodle allocates nothing and calculates no grades on its own when it switches. Changes what students can do: confirm with the person first.

tools.name: assess_workshop_submission
tools.description: Assess a workshop submission as the person, through the workshop's assessment form (its grading strategy's): a grade and comment per criterion in the form's order, overall feedback for the author (HTML), and any other field by name. A new assessment the first time, the same one changed after. Only in the assessment phase. Returns the grade it gives. The author reads it: confirm with the person first.

feedback.description: Overall feedback for the author (HTML); no aliases in it

fields.description: Any other field of the form, by name

tools.name: get_workshop_submission
tools.description: Read a workshop submission as its page shows it: title, text (HTML), attached files, author (an alias when the server pseudonymizes, where Moodle shows authors) and whether the person can edit it now. Without submissionId or author, the person's own (none when they haven't submitted); a teacher reads anyone's, a reviewer those allocated to them.

author.description: Or its author's alias, when the server pseudonymizes

authorId.description: Or its author's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: save_workshop_submission
tools.description: Add the person's submission to a workshop, or change the one they have, through its submission form: title, text (HTML, with local images embedded), attached local files; only what is given changes (a new one needs a title). Moodle takes it in the submission phase, within its dates. Returns the submission. Reviewers will read it: confirm with the person first.

title.description: Its title; a new one needs it

content.description: Its text (HTML), where the workshop takes online text; no aliases in it

attachments.description: Absolute local paths: they replace the files attached before

embed.description: Absolute local files to embed in the text, which names each by its file name:

tools.name: list_workshop_examples
tools.description: List a workshop's example submissions as its page shows a teacher: title, and whether its reference assessment is made, with its grade. Moodle lists them in the setup phase, where the workshop uses examples.

tools.name: add_workshop_example
tools.description: Add an example submission to a workshop, for participants to practise assessing: title, text (HTML, with local images embedded) and attached files. Then assess_workshop_example makes its reference assessment. Only where the workshop uses examples. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

content.description: Its text (HTML), where the workshop takes online text; no aliases in it

attachments.description: Absolute local paths: they replace the files attached before

embed.description: Absolute local files to embed in the text, which names each by its file name:

tools.name: edit_workshop_example
tools.description: Change an example submission: only what is given (attachments replace those there). Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

title.description: Its title; a new one needs it

content.description: Its text (HTML), where the workshop takes online text; no aliases in it

attachments.description: Absolute local paths: they replace the files attached before

embed.description: Absolute local files to embed in the text, which names each by its file name:

tools.name: delete_workshop_example
tools.description: Delete an example submission with its assessments (the reference one and participants' practice ones). Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

tools.description: Assess an example submission through the workshop's assessment form, as assess_workshop_submission does a submission: a teacher's assessment is the reference participants' are compared with; a participant's is their practice, where the workshop lets them assess examples now. Returns the grade it gives.

feedback.description: Overall feedback for the author (HTML); no aliases in it

fields.description: Any other field of the form, by name

tools.name: calculate_workshop_grades
tools.description: Calculate a workshop's grades in the evaluation phase, as "Re-calculate grades" does: each submission's grade from its assessments, each assessment's grade for assessing by the workshop's evaluation method, comparison its strictness. Overridden grades stay. Returns the submissions and assessments with their grades (people as aliases when the server pseudonymizes). Students will see the grades once the workshop is closed: confirm with the person first.

comparison.description: How strictly assessments are compared with the best one; the form keeps the last one used

tools.name: override_workshop_grade
tools.description: Override a grade Moodle calculated in a workshop: a submission's grade, or an assessment's grade for assessing (give one of the two ids, from get_workshop), with feedback for the author or the reviewer; remove: true takes the override away, so the calculated grade counts again. Returns the submission or assessment afterwards. Students see it: confirm with the person first.

grade.description: A whole number up to the workshop's grade for submission (or for assessment)

tools.name: get_workshop_allocation
tools.description: Read a workshop's allocation as its manual allocation page shows it (in the course's current group): each submission with its author and the reviewers allocated to it, and the participants who may be allocated as reviewers. People as aliases when the server pseudonymizes. Takes a teacher's role.

tools.name: allocate_workshop_reviewer
tools.description: Allocate a reviewer to a submission, as the manual allocation page's "Add reviewer" does, in any phase. The submission by its id or its author, the reviewer one get_workshop_allocation lists as a potential reviewer (aliases when the server pseudonymizes). A reviewer already allocated is left as is. Returns the submission's reviewers afterwards. The reviewer is given work: confirm with the person first.

submissionId.description: The submission, as get_workshop_allocation gives it; or its author

authorId.description: The submission's author's user id, when the server shows names

reviewer.description: The reviewer's alias, when the server pseudonymizes

reviewerId.description: The reviewer's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: remove_workshop_reviewer
tools.description: Remove a reviewer's allocation to a submission: Moodle deletes their assessment of it. An assessment already graded is only deleted with evenIfAssessed, and its grade is lost. Returns the submission's reviewers afterwards. Confirm with the person first.

submissionId.description: The submission, as get_workshop_allocation gives it; or its author

authorId.description: The submission's author's user id, when the server shows names

reviewer.description: The reviewer's alias, when the server pseudonymizes

reviewerId.description: The reviewer's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: allocate_workshop_randomly

tools.name: list_notifications
